## Purpose

This SOP describes the deployment, data retrieval, and barometric
compensation of Onset HOBO water level loggers for continuous
monitoring of water surface elevation in streams, lakes, wetlands, and
groundwater wells [@onset_u20l; @freeman2004]. Continuous stage records
are essential for developing stage-discharge rating curves,
characterizing hydrologic response to storms, and documenting seasonal
water table fluctuations.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Onset HOBO U20, U20L, and MX2001 water level loggers
  deployed at EA Program surface water and groundwater monitoring sites
- **Does not apply to:** Real-time telemetered stage recorders;
  acoustic or radar level sensors; staff gauge readings (visual
  observations recorded in the field notebook)
- **Location:** All EA Program hydrologic monitoring sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve deployment locations and logging intervals      |
| Trained Personnel | Deploy, retrieve, and download loggers per this SOP     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Absolute pressure:** Pressure measured relative to a perfect
  vacuum; the HOBO U20L measures absolute pressure (water column plus
  atmospheric), which must be compensated to isolate water-column
  pressure [@freeman2004].
- **Barometric compensation:** Post-processing step in HOBOware that
  subtracts a concurrent barometric pressure record (from a reference
  logger deployed in air) from the absolute pressure record to yield
  true water depth [@onset_hoboware].
- **Datum:** A fixed reference elevation (e.g., NAVD88, local
  benchmark) to which stage measurements are referenced.
- **Deployment depth:** The vertical distance from the water surface
  to the sensor face at the time of deployment; used as the initial
  reference for water-level calculations.
- **HOBO U20L:** Onset Computer Corporation submersible water-level
  logger recording absolute pressure and temperature at user-defined
  intervals; rated to a maximum depth of 9 m (model U20L-01) or 4 m
  (model U20L-04 barometric) [@onset_u20l].
- **HOBOconnect / HOBOware:** Onset software (mobile app and desktop,
  respectively) used to program loggers, download data, apply
  barometric compensation, and export time-series data
  [@onset_hoboware].
- **Stage:** Water-surface elevation at a monitoring location,
  expressed relative to a datum; the primary hydrologic quantity
  derived from pressure transducer records.
- **Stage-discharge rating curve:** An empirical relationship between
  stream stage and discharge (Q) at a gauging cross-section; enables
  conversion of continuous stage records into continuous discharge
  records [@freeman2004].
- **Stilling well:** A perforated pipe anchored in the stream or lake
  bed that protects the logger from direct current, debris, and
  disturbance while allowing free water exchange.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Deployment sites may involve steep banks, slippery
  surfaces, swift water, or confined spaces (well casings). Work in
  pairs at all stream and well sites.
- **Drowning:** Do not deploy loggers during high-flow events. Never
  wade in flows deeper than waist height.
- **Biological:** Waterborne pathogens; ticks and snakes in riparian
  areas.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Wading boots or chest waders (stream deployments)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes (well deployments)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Required Training

- [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd)
- Work with a trained partner for all in-stream deployments


## Instrument Specifications

### HOBO U20L Water Level Logger

| Parameter              | Value                                            |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| Measurement principle  | Absolute pressure (water + atmosphere)           |
| Pressure range         | 0--9 m (U20L-01) or 0--4 m barometric (U20L-04) |
| Accuracy               | +/- 0.1% full scale (~0.5 cm water)             |
| Logging interval       | 1 second to 18 hours (user-configurable)         |
| Memory                 | ~21,700 combined readings                        |
| Battery life           | ~5 years at 1-minute logging                     |
| Communication          | Optical USB coupler (U20L)                       |

### HOBO MX2001 Water Level Logger

| Parameter       | Value                                                   |
|:----------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Communication   | Bluetooth Low Energy; download via HOBOconnect app      |
| Pressure range  | 0--9 m or 0--4 m models                                |
| Other specs     | Similar to U20L                                         |

### Barometric Reference Logger

Because the water level loggers measure absolute pressure, a companion
barometric pressure logger must be deployed above the water surface at
or near the site. An Onset HOBO U20L-04 barometric model or HOBO MX
barometric logger serves this purpose.

## Estimated Time

| Task                               | Time             |
|:-----------------------------------|:-----------------|
| Logger programming (HOBOware)      | 10--15 min       |
| Stilling well installation (new)   | 30--90 min       |
| Logger deployment (existing site)  | 15--30 min       |
| Data retrieval and export          | 15--30 min       |
| Barometric compensation (HOBOware) | 15--30 min       |


## Procedure

### Logger Programming

1. Connect the logger to HOBOware using the optical USB coupler or
   open HOBOconnect via Bluetooth.
2. Select **Launch** (HOBOware) or **Configure** (HOBOconnect).
3. Set the logging interval appropriate to the project (5 min is
   typical for hydrologic studies; 15 min for long-term deployment).
4. Enable a delayed start if synchronizing with another logger at the
   site.
5. Record the logger serial number, launch time, and interval in the
   field notebook and in the deployment spreadsheet.

### Stream Deployment (Stilling Well)

1. Choose a stable bank location away from direct turbulence but
   representative of the cross-section stage.
2. Install the stilling well (2-inch PVC with perforations) vertically
   with the bottom anchored and the top above expected high-water level.
   Ensure the perforations face upstream and downstream.
3. Lower the logger into the stilling well and secure it with stainless
   steel wire or cable tie. The logger should hang freely.
4. Record the deployment elevation:
   - Distance from the top of the stilling well to the water surface
     and to the logger sensor
   - Staff gauge reading (if installed)
   - GPS coordinates per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd)
5. Deploy the barometric reference logger nearby, above the high-water
   line, in a shaded and ventilated location (e.g., inside a radiation
   shield attached to a tree or post). Do not seal it in an airtight
   container.
6. Photograph the deployment.

### Well Deployment

1. Remove the well cap and measure depth to water using an e-tape.
   Record the measurement.
2. Lower the logger into the well on stainless steel cable or braided
   fishing line. Position below the lowest expected water level but
   above the well screen bottom.
3. Secure the suspension cable to the well cap or casing.
4. Record the logger depth below the top of casing (TOC) and the TOC
   elevation if surveyed.
5. Replace the well cap.
6. Deploy the barometric reference logger at the wellhead or nearby.

### Data Retrieval

Retrieve data at intervals appropriate for the project (typically
monthly or quarterly).

**U20L (optical coupler):**

1. Remove the logger from the stilling well.
2. Attach the optical USB coupler and connect to the laptop.
3. In HOBOware, select **Readout**. The logger continues recording
   after readout.
4. Return the logger to its deployment position.

**MX2001 (Bluetooth):**

1. Open the HOBOconnect app on a smartphone within ~30 m line of sight.
2. Select the logger and tap **Readout**.
3. The logger does not need to be removed from the water.

### Barometric Compensation

1. In HOBOware, open the water level logger file and the barometric
   reference logger file.
2. Select **Data Assistant > Barometric Compensation**.
3. Specify the reference water level: enter a staff gauge reading or
   a known water surface elevation at a specific date and time.
4. HOBOware subtracts the barometric pressure from the absolute
   pressure to yield the water column height.
5. Export the compensated data as `.csv`.
6. Save using the convention: `YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_waterlevel_compensated.csv`.
7. Commit data to the project repository per
   [SOP-L801](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Verify that the barometric logger file overlaps the full duration of
  the water level record. Gaps in barometric data prevent compensation.
- Compare the compensated stage at the download visit against a
  simultaneous staff gauge reading. Acceptable agreement is within
  1 cm.
- Flag and investigate any sudden offsets or drift in the compensated
  record (may indicate logger movement, sedimentation, or battery
  failure).


## Data Management

1. Save all raw logger files (`.hobo`) to `data/raw/loggers/` in the
   project repository.
2. Save compensated `.csv` files to `data/processed/stage/`.
3. Commit all files per [SOP-L801](../lab_sops/SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd).

## Training Record

Before deploying water level loggers independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate logger programming (launch, interval, delayed start)
   using HOBOware or HOBOconnect
3. Participate in a supervised stream or well deployment
4. Demonstrate barometric compensation in HOBOware and export of
   compensated data
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
